fields.title: A revolution in the treatment of leukaemia
fields.bodyHtml:
Not long ago, scientists developed a way of dealing with cancer that sets the body to fight the malignant process by itself. The technique began to attract close attention when more than 90 per cent of terminally ill patients were found to have entered remission.

The treatment involves taking white blood cells from the patient's blood, modifying them and returning them to the bloodstream. To be precise, the immune cells affected by the viral or malignant process are taken (T-killer cells).

These cells are then modified, and in this way reprogrammed to recognise and block the disease process. The reprogrammed cells are introduced into the bloodstream and begin to act naturally, without outside intervention.

For the time being the technique is used in clinical practice as experimental and is offered in cases where other forms of treatment have brought no result. The outcome is striking in its effectiveness: more than 90 per cent of cases showed complete remission, with no cancerous cells remaining.

Leading scientists internationally note that the technique gives grounds for optimism, but that this is only the beginning. According to the specialists, the main task today is to work out how to adapt this principle of treatment to other forms of cancer.

fields.title: A robot instead of a scalpel
fields.bodyHtml:
The fast-developing field of surgical robotics is changing the face of modern surgery before our eyes. Israel is one of the world leaders in this field, and that is no accident.
Of all the surgical robots ever developed, only a handful of devices have been certified to date. Three of them were developed by Israelis.

According to Alon Wolf, founder and director of the Biorobotics and Biomechanics Laboratory at the Technion, Israel's institute of technology, the idea of surgical robotics arose from the need to give immediate medical help to soldiers on the battlefield without putting the surgeon at risk: ideally the intervention would be carried out under remote control from a bunker. That concept has still not been fully realised, but it gave a powerful impetus to the development of medical technology in this direction and is being used successfully in ordinary civilian medicine.

«Israeli developments, like American ones, are built on a body of knowledge from the military field,» explains Ziv Tamir, the first distributor of the Da Vinci surgical system in Israel. «That is what fundamentally distinguishes them from surgical robotics projects in other countries, which grow out of academic research and are not always directed at specific practical needs.»

Meet the certified Israeli inventions

Mazor Robotics of Caesarea is one of the world leaders in pioneering work on robot-assisted neurosurgery and spinal surgery. Its first product, SpineAssist, received FDA certification back in 2004. The next-generation device developed from it, the Renaissance Guidance System, is now in use in nearly 100 medical centres in various countries. The robot is used to take biopsies, for reconstructive operations, for the surgical correction of scoliosis, for spinal fusion and for other procedures demanding the highest precision.

The Flex Robotic System from MedRobotics, based on Alon Wolf's «snake robot», can reach cavities of the body that the surgeon cannot see directly. This matters particularly in head and neck surgery.

MST (Medical Surgery Technologies) makes AutoLap, a video-guided system for positioning the laparoscope optimally, which helps the surgeon orient themselves and steadies their movements. The surgeon wears a wireless ring-shaped device on the index finger that communicates with the AutoLap system. Dedicated software captures and interprets the visual information coming from the laparoscope and manoeuvres in step with the surgeon's hand signals in real time. «We compare this system to an Xbox in clinical practice,» explains Moti Frimer, the company's director. «The system understands gestures. Where most robotic systems are controlled with joysticks or other devices, MST responds directly to the movement of the surgeon's hand.»

Now a look into the near future of medicine worldwide: four Israeli inventions, one of them going through certification and three still in development

Human Extensions has developed an ergonomic bionic surgical glove that improves the precision and smoothness of movement. The device is currently going through FDA certification in the United States and CE certification in the European Union. According to Tami Frenkel, the company's director, it can be fitted to a particular surgeon and a particular task. «This pioneering solution will for the first time allow surgeons to perceive the patient's anatomy directly, in the way it is understood during open surgery,» Frenkel stresses, «as though the surgeon's hands were inside the patient's body.»

Microbot Medical, founded in 2010, is developing two pioneering devices, ViRob and TipCAT. ViRob is an autonomous micro-robot, rather like a submarine, that allows the surgeon to send a video camera, a drug or a shunt into the narrowest and least accessible places in the body (blood vessels, organs of the digestive or respiratory system) and to carry out minimally invasive interventions under MRI or CT guidance. TipCAT is a flexible self-propelled endoscope for use in the colon, the blood vessels and the urinary tract. Safe, quick and gentle movement inside the structures of the body is achieved by inflating and deflating the «balloons» — the sections of the probe — one after another.

XACT Robotics is currently developing a robotic system for inserting and steering a needle precisely during minimally invasive procedures under CT guidance, such as a lung biopsy. Any departure from the planned path, however small, is detected immediately and corrected without the need to reinsert the needle or reposition the patient.

Original source: https://www.doktorisrael.ru

fields.title: Expert advice: how to get better without spending on expensive medicines
fields.bodyHtml:
Summer is over and the cold weather is already closing in fast. The arrival of autumn always brings a weakening of the immune system and, as a result, colds and flu. How can the illness be kept from taking hold without spending on expensive preparations? A group of medical experts has the answer: «Do not rush to take expensive antibiotics at the first stage of the illness.»

Taking antibiotics for a cold is a very common mistake among people in almost every country. Even where there is a viral infection, it is not advisable to take them at the initial stage. The only exception may be an advanced illness or complications.

Nor is it advisable to combine preparations with similar effects. One antipyretic, one nasal preparation and tablets for a sore throat are enough. It should be noted that a person with a cold needs plenty of vitamins. They need not come in the form of preparations, since we obtain most beneficial substances from fresh fruit and vegetables.

To avoid seasonal illness, doctors recommend giving time to preventing viral infections through vaccination, which removes the risk of falling ill and saves money on treatment.
